title: Packing Unit Squares in a Square of Side Just Below an Integer: A Window Bound, 5308 Improved Bounds, and the Structure of Best-Known Packings
content: Let s(n) be the side of the smallest square containing n non-overlapping unit squares. For sides just below an integer K, recent preprints show that s(n) < K for all n ≤ K² − O(√K) and beyond, using an L-shaped packing: a grid with two tilted bands along adjacent walls. Using this construction, found here independently, we prove that for every integer K ≥ 16 the wasted area is at most 8√K + 19 at every side in [K − 1/K, K). Thicker bands also beat the grid, with waste of order K2/3. Optimized instances with rational angles and exact certificates, at sides in [K − 1/2, K), improve the best-known upper bound for 5308 values of n between 1182 and 9944. They beat the grid down to a fractional side that decreases from 0.62 at K = 35 to below 1/2 for K ≥ 78. A structural study of the best-known packings with n ≤ 1000 gives conjectures on tilted squares and tilt regimes, tested on 5077 packings with 1000 < n ≤ 10000.
